text: PLE fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months — Fitting the power-law exponential (PLE) time-rate relation q = qhat_i*exp(-Dhat_i*t^n/(n*Dhat_i + Dhat_inf)) (A.11) to the 48 monthly oil rates of TX well 42-329-41743 (45492.0 bbl in month 1 down to 5046.0 bbl in month 48), with qhat_i fixed at the observed month-1 rate of 45492.0 bbl and the remaining three parameters fitted, gives Dhat_i = 0.04194 1/month, n = 0.588577, Dhat_inf = 0.130009 1/month, with R-squared = 0.909838 (SSE = 290290515.794072 bbl^2, max abs residual = 10802.980507 bbl). No parameter is pinned at a bound: Dhat_i = 0.04194, n = 0.588577 and Dhat_inf = 0.130009 all sit strictly inside their fit ranges, with Dhat_inf = 0.130009 1/month carrying the limiting term the paper credits with curbing PLE's EUR over-estimation (p06). The largest single residual is at month 1 (10802.980507 bbl, about 23.7% of the month-1 rate), where the curve's t = 0 initial-rate convention lags the measured first monthly average. (why: The paper's nomenclature (p10) defines qhat_i as the initial rate coefficient, and the paper warns that sole reliance on regression for time-rate analysis leads to non-uniqueness (p05); with 48 monthly points and 4 free parameters the PLE regression is not unique on this well (an unconstrained fit runs qhat_i to the arbitrary 1e6 bound), so anchoring qhat_i to the measured month-1 rate is the paper-consistent fix. What remains is a fully identified 3-parameter curve for EUR work: R-squared 0.909838 over the pre-staleness 48-month window with a built-in limit on late-time decline (Dhat_inf = 0.130009 1/month, the same guard the paper singles out for PLE and modified-hyperbolic, p06). An analyst can now use the fitted q(t) directly for 30-year EUR work (p06-p07) and should refit a longer window once the 7-month feed staleness (TX 2026 volumes zero) is repaired.)
summary: PLE fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months

text: SE fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months — Fitting the stretched exponential (SE) model q = qhat_i*exp(-(t/tau)^n) (A.15) to the same 48 months of TX 42-329-41743, with qhat_i fixed at the observed month-1 rate of 45492.0 bbl and (tau, n) fitted, gives tau = 9.185146 months, n = 0.588579, with R-squared = 0.909838 (SSE = 290290515.790746 bbl^2, max abs residual = 10802.916777 bbl). No parameter is pinned at a bound: tau = 9.185146 months sits well inside its [1, 500] fit range, and the largest residual is at month 1 (10802.916777 bbl, about 23.7% of the month-1 rate). (why: With qhat_i anchored, SE is nearly a twin of the anchored PLE on these rows (SE SSE 290290515.790746 bbl^2 vs PLE SSE 290290515.794072 bbl^2, with matching exponents n = 0.588579 vs 0.588577), exactly the paper's expectation that PLE and SE results are 'very similar (as should be expected)' because SE is PLE's Dhat_inf = 0 limit (p06-p07). The anchored R-squared of 0.909838 carries the month-1 anchoring residual of 10802.916777 bbl: the price of an honest, non-arbitrary initial rate. An analyst would not extrapolate SE beyond the data without a terminal constraint, since SE carries no limiting term of its own.)
summary: SE fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months

text: MH fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months, Dlim fixed at 0.05 1/month — Fitting the modified hyperbolic (MH) model - hyperbolic q = qi*(1 + b*Di*t)^(-1/b) for t <= texp, then exponential at terminal decline Dlim fixed to 0.05 1/month (A.1, A.6) - to the 48 months of TX 42-329-41743 gives qi = 79621.36345, Di = 0.812595 1/month, b = 1.454016, texp = 47.0 (pinned at its 47 upper bound), with R-squared = 0.98831 (SSE = 37637254.805154 bbl^2, max abs residual = 2803.502521 bbl). The fit puts b = 1.454016 above 1 and pushes texp to the final month of data, so inside the fitted window the model is effectively a pure b > 1 hyperbola with no exponential tail yet active. (why: This is exactly the regime the paper warns about: unconstrained hyperbolic extrapolation with b > 1 overstates reserves, and the only thing keeping this MH forecast finite is the fixed Dlim = 0.05 1/month tail beyond texp (p06-p07, p10 nomenclature). An analyst using this fit must keep the terminal-decline constraint, treat the b > 1 branch as valid only up to texp, and cross-check the 30-year EUR against PLE, whose Dhat_inf term limits over-estimation the same way.)
summary: MH fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months, Dlim fixed at 0.05 1/month

text: DNG fit, TX 42-329-41743, first 48 producing months — Fitting the Duong model q = q1*Gp^(m/(1-m))/(1 + a*t)^(1/(1-m)) (A.20), whose base concept is a linear q/Gp-t trend on log-log (A.24), to the 48 months of TX 42-329-41743 gives q1 = 50403.974163, a = 0.291353 1/month, m = 0.01 (pinned at its 0.01 lower bound), with R-squared = 0.968593 (SSE = 101120330.038221 bbl^2, max abs residual = 2942.248871 bbl). With m at its bound the Gp-dependent factor q1*Gp^(m/(1-m)) is essentially a constant, so the fit reduces to a plain (1 + a*t)^(-1) shape rather than the full Duong form. (why: Duong's model was developed for tight gas and rests on a linear q/Gp-t trend on log-log (A.24); the paper's Field B - depletion-dominated data where 'it is not clear that a linear trend ever fully exists' - concludes the Duong model 'may be the least appropriate model' for that play (p05, p07). The m-at-boundary collapse here is the same diagnostic on this oil well, and DNG has no limiting term, so the paper notes its EUR estimates should (almost always) run above the other models' and the discrepancy is largest for depletion-dominated data (p06, p08). text: Rows above 100% of initial oil rate persist into late life: 2.1M TX and 1.8M NM rows past month 36 — In decline_curve_inputs, 5,110,833 rows have oil_rate_pct_of_initial > 100 (TX 3,302,077; NM 1,808,180; OK just 576).
